info.title: Netskope REST API v2
info.description: Netskope REST API v2 — curated Integration Model covering the customer-facing operations for events, alerts, datasearch, policy, steering/NPA, CASB, SaaS Posture Management, incidents, profiles, infrastructure, SCIM, reporting, and more.
info.x-itential-curated: Sourced from Netskope's official api-schemas repo published via Postman (postman.com/netskope-tech-alliances/netskope-rest-api) and mirrored at github.com/joshblease/netskope-apiv2-oas. Curated to customer-facing operations — excludes internal UI microservices (ui, echo, dem, adem) and niche/specialized services (nsiq, skopilot, forwardproxy, drm, foundation, ubadatasvc). Full spec available in netskope_v2.json.

get.summary: Get Destination Profiles
get.description:
Get a subset of Destination Profiles restricted by offset, limit, and filter.
The returned profiles can be filtered by one or more attributes.
The basic syntax is: attribute attribute_operator "value" or attribute in ("value1", "value2") for "in" attribute operator.
  • Supported attributes (case-sensitive): id, name, status, values, description
  • Supported attribute operators: eq (equal: case-sensitive fully match), in(in array of strings, limited to 10 strings: case-sensitive fully match), co (contains: case-insensitive partial match).
  • Supported value type: string, which must be enclosed with double quotes.
    • Examples:
    1. Find a profile name contains "eng": ?filter=name co "eng".
    2. Find a profile status in "pending" or "pending-delete": ?filter=status in ("pending","pending-delete").
    3. Find profiles whose id is 1 or 2 or 3: ?filter=id in ("1","2","3").
    4. Find profiles whose values contains "netskope": ?filter=values co "netskope".
    5. Find profiles whose values equal "www.netskope.com": ?filter=values eq "www.netskope.com".
    6. Find profiles whose values is either "www.netskope.com" or "www.example.com": ?filter=values in ("www.netskope.com","www.example.com").

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Specifying fields to be returned in the response. Example: ?fields=name,description. Note that the id field will always be returned. If omitted, all fields will be returned.

parameters.description: The (zero-based) offset of the first item in the list to retrieve. Default to 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max number of items to retrieve. Default to 10. Maximum 50.

parameters.name: filter

get.summary: Get a subset of Service Profiles restricted by offset, limit, and filter. The returned profiles can be filtered by one or more attributes.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
The basic syntax is:

  1. Attribute operator "Value"
  2. Attribute in ("value1", "value2") for "in" attribute operator.

  1. Supported attributes (case-insensitive): id, name, status, type, and description.
  2. Supported attribute operators (case-insensitive): eq (equals), sw (starts with), in, and co (contains).
  3. Supported value type (case-insensitive): string, which must be enclosed with double quotes.
  4. Supported logical operators (case-insensitive): and.

For example, to filter returned profiles to only show records with ID 1, 2, or 3:
?filter=id in ("1","2","3").


You can also filter multiple attributes by adding an and logical operator and another attribute in the same format as the previous example.


For example, to show records whose name start with "prod" and whose description contain "service":
?filter=name sw "prod" and description co "service".

post.summary: Given a file object, traverse the data lineage graph either forward or backward according to params
post.description:
The API supports two ways to supply the file object to start the lineage traversal.
The first method is to provide a ClickhouseAppEvent JSON structure in the request body. The schema should
be unmodified from what Clickhouse returns in a query. If using this method, the client must provide the tenant
id in the header. The API will extract and use the file object from the provided input.
The second method is to provide the unique ID used internally by the service in the query parameter. The typical
scenario to use this method is to do a follow-up query after a previous lineage request, to further
expand the lineage graph from a node returned by the previous request. The unique ID is a part of the
response. If both the unique ID and the event is supplied, the API will use the unique ID and ignore the
event.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the file to start the graph traversal. For example: 97c5268fc09233f886ca377df1e3f83f6a026c3895bcb0e38cd85a116b1e3c36

parameters.name: inferred
parameters.description: Control whether the traversal includes inferred lineage. Default is true. For example: true

parameters.name: forward
parameters.description: Control whether to traverse forward or backwards. Forward traversal finds descendents. Default is true. For example: true

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Control whether to include debug info in the response. If set to false, only pretty_nodes and pretty_relations are returned. Otherwise, all fields are returned. Default is false. For example: true

requestBody.description: In the absence of the id param, supply the event for the service to retrieve lineage of the file object included in the event

200.description: The structure contains both raw nodes and edges as fetched from the database, as well as aggregated nodes and edges for easier representation

400.description: Bad request. Refer to the error string for more information

post.summary: Request to infer lineages of all files in the given location
post.description:
The primary way to infer lineage is via periodically database scans. This API provides a backup way to
run tests, or to start the inference immediately without waiting for the next database scan. Location is
the concept to limit the scope of one inference task. A location can be a SaaS app, a host, or a device.
Lineage inference does not occur between files in different locations, e.g., between a file in SaaS app and
a file on a host. Rather, their lineage is directly observed from app events (out of scope of this API).

requestBody.description: The inference task specifying the location and other metadata. Only 1 of the 3 locations should be set: app:instance pair, host, or device

200.description: The inference task is processed successfully

204.description: The inference task is skipped because the same task is already running
